i.norm: Sample text strings covering different Unicode ranges to exercise encoding detection. Each constant is named after the smallest charset that can represent it.
Combined text requiring a Unicode-capable encoding such as UTF-8 or UTF-16.

Builds an XML document string, optionally with an explicit encoding declaration. @param text the body text to embed inside {@code <text>…</text>} @param encoding the encoding to declare in the XML prolog, or {@code null} for no declaration @return a well-formed XML string

Writes {@code xml} through an {@link XmlStreamWriter} configured with {@code defaultEncodingName}, then verifies that:
  1. The writer chose {@code encodingName} as its active charset.
  2. The active charset can represent {@code encodingName} (contains check).
  3. The bytes written to the stream match {@code xml} encoded with {@code encodingName}.
@param xml the raw XML string to write @param encodingName the encoding that should be detected/chosen by the writer @param defaultEncodingName the default encoding to configure on the writer (may be {@code null})
writerAfterClose is intentionally read after the try-with-resources block
Keep a reference outside the block so we can inspect the writer's chosen encoding after close() has been called (close() finalises charset detection).
Convenience overload that uses {@code null} as the default encoding (the writer will then fall back to UTF-8).

Builds an XML document from {@code text} and {@code encoding}, then delegates to {@link #checkXmlContent} with the encoding that should actually be used.

When {@code encoding} is {@code null} (no prolog declaration), the writer relies on {@code defaultEncoding}; if that is also {@code null}, UTF-8 is the ultimate fallback.

@param text body text for the XML document @param encoding encoding declared in the XML prolog, or {@code null} @param defaultEncoding default encoding to configure on the writer, or {@code null}

Determine which encoding the writer is expected to choose: 1. Declared in the prolog → use prolog encoding 2. No prolog, but default → use the configured default 3. No prolog and no default → fall back to UTF-8

Verifies that {@link XmlStreamWriter} selects the correct default encoding when the XML document has no explicit encoding declaration in its prolog.

Scenarios covered (all use {@code encoding=null}, so the prolog carries no declaration):

  • No default encoding specified → writer falls back to UTF-8
  • Default encoding = UTF-8 → writer uses UTF-8
  • Default encoding = UTF-16 → writer uses UTF-16
  • Default encoding = UTF-16BE → writer uses UTF-16BE
  • Default encoding = ISO-8859-1 → writer uses ISO-8859-1
No prolog declaration, no configured default → expect UTF-8 fallback
No prolog declaration; default encoding is UTF-8 → expect UTF-8
No prolog declaration; default encoding is UTF-16 → expect UTF-16
No prolog declaration; default encoding is UTF-16BE → expect UTF-16BE
No prolog declaration; default encoding is ISO-8859-1 → expect ISO-8859-1
